page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Optimized3.Flex.2-16 is a virtual machine offering within the Optimized family, powered by a 3.0 GHz Intel Xeon 6354 processor based on the x86_64 architecture. The instance allocates 4 vCPUs derived from 2 dedicated physical cores with 2 threads per core. System memory is provisioned at 16.0 GB, yielding a 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU.

The instance includes no bundled local storage, requiring attached remote block volumes for persistent data storage and operating system installations. Networking provisions include 1 complimentary public IPv4 address. The configuration contains 0 GPUs, relying entirely on the host Intel Xeon CPU for computational tasks. Dedicated core allocation ensures that compute resources are not shared across neighboring tenants.

Because the VM.Optimized3.Flex.2-16 provides a balanced ratio of 4 vCPUs to 16 GB RAM, it serves workloads such as application middleware, web serving, microservices, and general compute tasks. Without onboard NVMe storage, workloads demanding high continuous local I/O must account for network storage latency, while memory-heavy or hardware-accelerated processing tasks require different instance classes.

These specifications position the server for standard enterprise tasks, including web serving, application middleware, background job processing, and containerized microservice deployments.
